questions.text:
Which of the following statements about a relation R in first normal form (1NF)
is/are TRUE ?
questions.solution:
1NF only requires every attribute value to be atomic (no multi-valued or composite attributes).

- R can have a multi-attribute key [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE (e.g. key (roll_no, course_id)). This is about keys, not about values.
- R cannot have a foreign key [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE, 1NF puts no restriction on foreign keys.
- R cannot have a composite attribute [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE, a composite attribute is non-atomic and must be split into simple attributes.
- R cannot have more than one candidate key [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: R can have a multi-attribute key; R cannot have a composite attribute

questions.text: Let S be the specification: "Instructors teach courses. Students register for courses. Courses are allocated classrooms. Instructors guide students." Which one of the following ER diagrams CORRECTLY represents S?
questions.solution:
From the specification we need 4 entity sets [latex]\text{---}[/latex] Instructor, Course, Student, Classroom [latex]\text{---}[/latex] and 4 relationships:
Instructor-Teaches-Course, Student-Registers-Course, Course-Allocated-Classroom, Instructor-Guides-Student.

- (i): Registration is drawn as an entity and Student as a relationship [latex]\text{---}[/latex] wrong.
- (ii): no Student entity; an extra Projects entity is used [latex]\text{---}[/latex] wrong.
- (iii): Classroom is attached directly to Course and the Allocation relationship does not connect Classroom [latex]\text{---}[/latex] wrong.
- (iv): all four entities and all four relationships are connected correctly.

Answer: (iv)

questions.text:
Consider a database of fixed-length records, stored as an ordered file. The database has 25,000 records, with each record being 100 bytes, of which the primary key occupies 15 bytes. The data file is block-aligned in that each data record is fully contained within a block. The database is indexed by a primary index file, which is also stored as a block-aligned ordered file. The figure below depicts this indexing scheme.

Suppose the block size of the file system is 1024 bytes, and a pointer to a block occupies 5 bytes. The system uses binary search on the index file to search for a record with a given key. You may assume that a binary search on an index file of [latex]b[/latex] blocks takes [latex]\left \lceil \log_2 b \right \rceil [/latex] block accesses in the worst case.
Given a key, the number of block accesses required to identify the block in the data file that may contain a record with the key, in the worst case, is _____
questions.solution:
Compute the index size step by step:
- Records per data block = [latex]\lfloor1024/100\rfloor=10[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] data blocks = 25000 / 10 = 2500.
- Primary (sparse) index has one entry per data block: 2500 entries of [latex]15+5=20[/latex] bytes.
- Entries per index block = [latex]\lfloor1024/20\rfloor=51[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] index blocks = [latex]\lceil2500/51\rceil=50[/latex].

Binary search on the index: [latex]\lceil\log_2 50\rceil=6[/latex] block accesses identify the data block.

Answer: 6

questions.text:
Consider the following table named Student in a relational database. The primary key of this table is rollNum.
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \\ rollNum&name&gender&marks \\ \hline 1&Naman&M&62\\ \hline 2&Aliya&F&70 \\ \hline 3&Aliya &F&80 \\ \hline 4&James&M&82\\ \hline 5&Swati&F&65\\ \hline \end{array} [/latex]
The SQL query below is executed on this database.

SELECT *
FROM Student
WHERE gender = 'F' AND
 marks > 65;

The number of rows returned by the query is ______
questions.solution:
Rows with gender = 'F' and marks [latex]\gt[/latex] 65:
- Aliya, 70 True
- Aliya, 80 True
- Swati, 65 False (65 is not greater than 65)

SELECT * returns full rows, so the duplicate name does not matter.

Answer: 2

questions.text:
Which one of the options given below refers to the degree (or arity) of a relation in
relational database systems?
questions.solution:
Degree (arity) = number of attributes (columns) in the relation schema.
The number of tuples (rows) is called the cardinality.

Answer: Number of attributes of its relation schema

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Number of attributes of its relation schema.
Number of tuples stored in the relation.
Number of entries in the relation.
Number of distinct domains of its relation schema.
